name: Juice Shop: SQL Injection Login Bypass
short_description: Bypass authentication in OWASP Juice Shop using SQL injection.
description: OWASP Juice Shop is a modern web application with 100+ security challenges. This lesson covers the classic SQL injection login bypass - one of the first challenges. You'll learn how improper input sanitization leads to authentication bypass.
handler_message:
This is it. The final piece.

Cerberus runs a legitimate-looking e-commerce operation at 172.20.0.30. On the surface, it's a juice shop. Underneath, it's the financial clearinghouse for NIGHTFALL.

Every shell company transaction. Every offshore transfer. Every payment to operatives and contractors. It all flows through here, disguised as smoothie purchases.

SQL injection bypasses the login. Get admin access. Find the real transaction records.

You have everything else. The target list. The false flag evidence. The authorization chain.

This is where you find out who PROMETHEUS is. Who's paying for all of this. And then you have everything you need.

The clock is running. Go.
episode_intro:
The target list burns in your mind. Power stations. Water facilities. Financial systems. Real places. Real infrastructure. Real people who will die if this succeeds.

72 hours. That's all you have left.

Everything you've gathered - the deployment manifests, the false flag evidence, the authorization documents - it's enough to prove NIGHTFALL exists. But it's not enough to stop it.

You need to know who's behind this. Not just Cerberus. Someone is funding them. Someone with enough resources to orchestrate an attack on this scale and enough influence to ensure it's blamed on a foreign power.

PROMETHEUS. That's the codename. The primary investor whose money made all of this possible.

The Juice Shop storefront is their financial laundry. Millions of dollars disguised as fruit smoothie orders. SQL injection gets you past the login. Admin access gets you to the real records.

This is the endgame. Find PROMETHEUS. Expose everything. Or watch helplessly as NIGHTFALL goes live.
episode_outro:
The admin panel reveals the truth.

Transaction records stretching back three years. Payments tagged with project codes - SCADA-BRIDGE, ATTRIBUTION-PKG, NIGHTFALL-STAGING. Amounts that dwarf anything a juice shop could legitimately process.

And there, in the executive compensation records: the wire transfers to PROMETHEUS.

The account number routes to a law firm in Delaware. The law firm is owned by a trust in the Caymans. The trust's beneficial owner is...

A United States Senator.

Someone with access to classified briefings. Someone who sits on the Intelligence Committee. Someone who's been pushing for aggressive action against China for years.

NIGHTFALL isn't just a false flag operation. It's a manufactured justification for a war that certain people have wanted for decades.

You save everything. Screenshots. Transaction logs. The full money trail from offshore accounts to a sitting member of Congress.

Your connection drops. The screen goes black.

When it comes back, there's a message. Plain text. No sender.

'You have everything. 72 hours until NIGHTFALL. Choose carefully what you do with it.'

The cursor blinks. Waiting.

What you do next is up to you.

interstitial.title: Episode 8: STOREFRONT
interstitial.content:
PREVIOUSLY: The SQL injection revealed NIGHTFALL's target list. Power substations. Water treatment plants. Financial clearinghouses. Dates. Times. Coordinates.

This isn't theoretical anymore. The attack is scheduled. And you're running out of time to stop it.

You've gathered evidence of the conspiracy - deployment manifests, false flag markers, authorization chains. But you still don't know who's really behind this. Who's paying for an attack on American infrastructure?

PROMETHEUS. The primary investor. Their money flows through a front operation at 172.20.0.30 - a legitimate-looking e-commerce site disguised as a juice shop.

SQL injection bypasses the login. Admin access reveals the real records.

This is the endgame. Find PROMETHEUS. Expose everything.

steps.title: Open Juice Shop
steps.narrative: Juice Shop looks legitimate - a modern e-commerce site selling fruit beverages. Built on Node.js with Angular frontend. Underneath, it's a deliberately vulnerable application used for security training. Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser. For NIGHTFALL, it represents Cerberus's financial front.

steps.title: Find the login page
steps.narrative: Navigate to Account > Login. Standard authentication form. Email and password. Behind this form is a database query that validates credentials. If the query isn't properly parameterized, you can inject SQL commands.

steps.title: Test for SQL injection
steps.narrative: Classic injection payload. The single quote closes the email string. OR 1=1 makes the condition always true. -- comments out the password check. If vulnerable, this logs you in as the first user in the database - typically admin.

steps.title: Bypass login as admin
steps.narrative: More targeted attack. We know the admin email (from reconnaissance or guessing). The comment after the email bypasses password validation entirely. The query becomes: SELECT * FROM users WHERE email='admin@juice-sh.op'-- AND password='...'

steps.title: Alternative: First user bypass
steps.narrative: If you don't know the admin email, this broader injection works. The OR 1=1 returns all users; the application logs you in as the first one. On most systems, the first user is the administrator.

steps.title: View the scoreboard
steps.narrative: Juice Shop gamifies security testing - it tracks your progress through 100+ challenges. Open http://localhost:3000/#/score-board to see which vulnerabilities you've discovered. SQL injection login bypass should now be checked.

steps.title: Use SQLMap for automated testing
steps.narrative: SQLMap automates SQL injection discovery and exploitation. It tests multiple injection techniques and identifies the database type. The --batch flag accepts defaults instead of prompting. This is reconnaissance at scale.

steps.title: Extract database info
steps.narrative: List all databases. Juice Shop uses SQLite - a file-based database common in smaller applications. The transaction records, user data, and PROMETHEUS payment information are all stored here.

success_criteria: You've bypassed authentication and gained admin access to the Cerberus financial front. You can now access transaction records and trace the PROMETHEUS payments.
next_steps: Try other Juice Shop challenges: XSS, broken access control
